title: Bromodeoxyuridine \(BrdU) labeling and immunohistochemical detection in adult zebrafish brain
protocol: Prepare a 10 mg/mL stock BrdU solution in water.
Aliquot the BrdU solution and store at -20°C.
Thaw the BrdU aliquots in a 37°C water bath when needed.
Equilibrate the syringe with sterile water carefully to avoid air introduction.
Place 0.2 mg of BrdU solution per gram of fish body weight on parafilm.
Slowly take up the BrdU from parafilm into the equilibrated syringe.
Transfer the fish to an insulator ice bucket filled halfway with aquarium water.
Add ice cubes made from aquarium water until the temperature drops to 12°C.
Cool your fingertips in 12°C water and gently handle the immobilized fish.
Inject BrdU solution into the abdominal cavity of the fish.
Release the fish back into a 25°C system water tank and observe for 10 minutes.
Leave the fish in the tank for 4 to 24 hours post-injection.
Prepare an ice-water mixture with 4 parts ice and 1 part water in an ice bucket.
Place the fish completely in the ice-water mixture until movement ceases after 10 minutes.
Kill the fish by cutting its head using a scalpel once movement stops.
Put the fish head into fixation buffer immediately after decapitation.
Incubate the fish head in the fixation buffer at 4°C overnight.
Fill a 10 cm dish with PBS and add the fish or the fish head into the PBS.
Perform dissection using dumont tweezers under the dissecting microscope to clean all gills and fat tissue, removing pigments by peeling the thin membrane on the dorsal side of the brain.
Add the dissected brain in PBS into a 2 ml tube.
Wash samples 3 times with PBS-T for 5 min each, aspirating medium carefully and slowly adding new medium between washes.
Incubate brains 4 min in 30% methanol in PBS-T.
Incubate brains 4 min in 50% methanol in PBS-T.
Incubate brains 4 min in 70% methanol in PBS-T.
Incubate brains 4 min in 90% methanol in PBS-T.
Add 100% methanol and incubate at -20°C overnight for long-term storage if necessary.
Take brains from -20°C, equilibrate with room temperature methanol by washing once.
Incubate brains 4 min in 90% methanol in PBS-T during rehydration series.
Incubate brains 4 min in 70% methanol in PBS-T.
Incubate brains 4 min in 50% methanol in PBS-T.
Incubate brains 4 min in 30% methanol in PBS-T.
Wash with PBS-T and leave on rotator for 15 min.
Prepare 3% agarose in PBS, allowing to cool down to a temperature that the bottle can be held comfortably but not solidified.
Transfer cooled agarose into molds.
Pick each brain with tweezers and carefully drop into the agarose.
Adjust the orientation of the brains quickly using a bent syringe without touching them.
Release the agarose from the mould when it has set.
Cut the agarose into a small block in which the brain is at the center, ensuring it’s not close to the edges.
Attach the agarose blocks to the vibratome plate using a strong, water-based adhesive.
Fill the vibratome tank with PBS and mount the plate into the tank.
Start cutting slices of 50 μm thickness.
Transfer each slice into a 48-well plate filled with PBS after each cutting; two slices can be put into one well.
Wash all slices twice with PBS-T by aspirating the medium carefully without touching the slices.
Add 180 μL 2N HCl to each well and incubate at 37°C for 30 min without shaking.
Aspirate HCl from the wells and wash once with borate buffer.
Wash the wells three times with PBS-T, five minutes each on a rotator.
Incubate in blocking solution: 3% goat serum in PBS-T for one hour at room temperature on a rotator.
Prepare anti-BrdU antibody in blocking solution at a 1:500 dilution; mix well.
Add 180 μL of the antibody to each well except for the no-antibody control wells, which receive only blocking solution.
Leave plates at 4°C on a rotator for 24 to 72 hours.
Cover plates with parafilm to prevent evaporation.
Take plates out of the fridge and discard antibodies.
Wash plates three times with PBS-T, five minutes each.
Wash plates two times with PBS-T, fifteen minutes each.
Incubate in blocking solution: 3% goat serum in PBS-T for thirty minutes on a rotator.
Prepare secondary antibody in PBS-T at 1:1000 dilution and mix well.
Incubate at room temperature for two hours on the rotator.
Discard antibodies.
Wash plates three times with PBS-T, five minutes each.
Wash plates two times with PBS-T, fifteen minutes each.
Add 180 μL of 7-AAD working solution to the wells and incubate for ten minutes on a rotator.
Wash with PBS-T twice.
Fill a 15 cm dish with PBS and dip one microscope slide into it.
Incline slide to edge of plate, take two slices at a time from plate using brush and drop into PBS in dish.
Align slices onto microscope slide using no:0 brush; do not allow slices to wrap or dry.
Wipe dry excess water but let slices air dry without completely drying out.
Drop minute amounts of Prolong antifade reagent to each slice and also to the bottom of the slide.
Touch the coverslip to the edge of the slide and lower slowly onto the slices.
Leave the slides overnight at room temperature, in the dark.
Seal the edges with nail polish.
